doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: How clients hire him and writing for orchestra versus small horn section
summary: Singers call him directly; he is not part of the music business, orchestras faded with record companies, and he prefers a full orchestra.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you have a person, a manager, someone between you and potential work? If an up- and-coming singer said, “Oh I sure wish we could get Alan Broadbent to write strings for us” do they call you directly or do you have someone who handles that?

No they call me directly. I’m not part of the music business. I never really was. People think I’m writing all this music but as I said all that died with the record companies not wanting to foot the bill. And so orchestras kind of died with it. But there is a way to keep that going and to schmooze and play the whole scene, and you know write other kinds of material, I never could. So people recognize something in me and they like it or —
Is it harder to write a horn section part, let’s say three horns than it is to have a whole orchestra at your disposal?
I’d rather have the orchestra. Yeah. Yeah I can see that it would be a challenge of course.
